name: Suki AI
short_description: Premium AI voice assistant + ambient scribe with EHR commands for 100+ specialties. $299-399/mo makes it the most expensive mainstream option. Psychiatry supported but not the design focus.
long_description: Suki AI is a premium voice assistant and ambient scribe that combines documentation with voice commands for EHR navigation, ordering, and clinical Q&A. Unlike pure-ambient scribes, Suki enables hands-free chart interaction via bi-directional integration with Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, and MEDITECH Expanse. The platform supports 100+ medical specialties and 80+ languages, serving 400+ healthcare organizations. At $299-399/month per user, Suki is the most expensive mainstream AI scribe—significantly above Freed ($39-119/mo), Mentalyc ($20-120/mo), and Upheal ($1/session). Psychiatry is supported within multi-specialty coverage, but Suki captures broad narrative rather than psychiatry-specific elements; clinicians should expect to edit for diagnostic precision, MSE detail, and risk assessment language. FQHCs and community health centers may access special pricing.
one_liner: Premium voice assistant + ambient scribe with EHR commands. $299-399/mo—expensive but powerful.
best_for: Multi-specialty health systems needing voice commands + ambient scribe in one platform
Organizations on Epic, Cerner, athena, or MEDITECH wanting hands-free EHR navigation
Practices that can justify $299-399/mo per user for premium capabilities
Psychiatrists in enterprise settings where Suki is already deployed
not_for: Therapists doing psychotherapy—Suki doesn't understand therapy modalities
Solo or small practices—pricing is prohibitive vs. Freed, Mentalyc, Upheal
Budget-conscious practices—Suki costs 3-10x more than competitors

faqs.q: How much does Suki AI cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Suki Compose costs $299/month/user for ambient documentation. Suki Assistant costs $399/month/user and adds voice commands for EHR navigation, ordering, and clinical Q&A. This makes Suki the most expensive mainstream AI scribe—3-10x higher than Freed, Mentalyc, or Upheal.

faqs.q: Is Suki AI good for psychiatrists?
faqs.a: Suki supports psychiatry within its 100+ specialties, but it captures broad clinical narrative rather than psychiatry-specific elements. Expect to edit for diagnostic precision, MSE detail, and risk assessment language. Therapists should use Mentalyc or Upheal instead.

faqs.q: Which EHRs does Suki integrate with?
faqs.a: Suki has bi-directional, real-time integration with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, and MEDITECH Expanse. The integration enables voice commands for hands-free chart navigation.

faqs.q: Why is Suki AI so expensive?
faqs.a: Suki combines ambient documentation with voice-activated EHR commands—a dual capability most competitors don't offer. The voice assistant enables ordering, charting, and navigation without touching the keyboard. Whether this justifies 3-10x higher cost depends on workflow value.

faqs.q: Is there a cheaper alternative to Suki for mental health?
faqs.a: Yes. Freed ($39-119/mo) works for psychiatry medication management. Mentalyc ($20-120/mo) and Upheal ($1/session, capped $69/mo) are therapy-specific. All cost 80-95% less than Suki.
